A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study, despite the changed title and formatting. All main-text and supplementary material is readable, and corresponding methods, figures and tables can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original CodeT5 transfer experiments, F1/BLEU results, source-language ranking evaluations and feature-importance analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons and low-resource source-language analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain CodeT5-base fine-tuning and the LightGBM LambdaRank predictor with 100 trees, 16 leaves and four feature categories. The newly introduced regression and history methods are comparison baselines.

E1.justification: CodeNet, XCodeEval, the four task definitions and all Fig. 2 language grids are retained after renaming. However, v2 Table VII reports bf as a clone-detection source, absent from both versions' clone heatmap. Whether this represents added coverage, a previously undocumented experiment or a table error is unresolved.

E2.justification: v1 compares the proposed ranker against Dataset, Linguistic, Model and Syntax feature-category rankers in Fig. 4. v2 replaces these with a LightGBM regression-based ranker and a language-history shortest-path ranker in Fig. 3, substantially changing the RQ2 comparison set.

E3.justification: v1 Section 3.3 inconsistently assigns both 70K and 100K samples to code refinement. v2 Section III assigns 70K to error detection and 100K to clone detection and code repair. This corrects the reported setting without establishing reruns. F1/BLEU metrics and leave-one-target-out NDCG@3 evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the feature-category ablations across four tasks. It adds source-ranking analyses restricted to low-resource targets, using different common-source subsets (Tables VI–VII), and language-pair case analyses in Section IV-A and Table VIII. Sampling sensitivity and SHAP analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 3 reports means and standard deviations across language combinations; corresponding v2 Table II retains only means. Ranking figures still report mean and standard deviation across held-out target languages. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, and the many language-pair experiments are not repeated runs.

E6.justification: The central ranking results are revised through replacement baseline results, with regression exceeding the proposed ranker on clone detection in v2 Fig. 3. Some proposed-ranker means also shift, including compile/error detection from approximately 0.83 to 0.86. Tables VI–VII add low-resource aggregates, and Kotlin's mean rank changes from 2.5 to 2.0 in corresponding Tables 4/V. The four transfer heatmaps remain identical.

T1.justification: Neither version develops new theorems or proofs. v2 expands the explanation of SHAP and feature measurements without introducing substantively different mathematical reasoning or formal definitions.

C1.justification: The three contributions remain measuring multilingual transfer, predicting suitable source languages and identifying predictive language-pair features. The expanded abstract and introduction foreground findings already reported in v1 rather than redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds tentative explanations involving Kotlin's linguistic influences and C++'s difficulty, motivates low-resource-only source selection, and explicitly identifies the zero-target-training-data boundary. Its new internal-validity discussion also argues that many distinct language-pair experiments mitigate insufficient runs, an argument absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation through per-language linguistic-feature assignments in Table IX, explicit feature-measure encodings, Hugging Face implementation details and A100 training costs of 6–30 hours per source. These disclose previously unavailable inputs and implementation information. Code and model release remains a future promise in both versions.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Coursera source concerning Swift and Wolf et al.'s Hugging Face Transformers reference. The core transfer-learning literature and positioning relative to earlier programming-language studies remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and three task names, extensively rewrites the results narrative, adds introductory highlights and boxed takeaways, condenses the conclusion, and reorganizes quantitative/qualitative limitations into external/internal validity. These constitute substantial editing and restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, relocates existing result tables and the sampling figure to supplementary pages, redesigns ranking/SHAP displays and the feature table, and adds Tables VI–IX. The smaller transfer heatmaps now share a page, while their underlying images remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful implementation disclosures, regression/history comparisons and focused low-resource analyses. However, it removes feature-category controls and task-level dispersion, while new source-selection tables conflict with the unchanged heatmaps: bf in Table VII and the reversed Awk/Vim pair in Table VIII. These inconsistencies weaken the reliability of the practical recommendations being expanded, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
